gancho: Kamapuaʻa, the pig-man, comes to woo Pele at Kīlauea, and she calls him a pig and the son of a pig. Insults turn into a war of fire against rain: floods fill the crater, the fire sticks are saved, the grass burns, and the hog-god escapes as a fish. In the end, they split the island of Hawaiʻi in two. Based on Martha Beckwith, Hawaiian Mythology (1940), and W. D. Westervelt, Hawaiian Legends of Volcanoes (1916).
